title: Coordinate System Explorer
description: A labeled p5.js pixel grid with a live mouseX and mouseY readout, clickable markers, and challenges that ask for a point at a given height on a meter scale, after which the sim draws the correct point and shows the map() call, including the y flip, with the numbers filled in.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: p5.js
Coordinate Systems
map() Function
Screen Coordinates
publisher: MicroSims 2.0: Generating, Instrumenting and Evaluating Interactive Learning Objects with AI

educational.topic: The p5.js coordinate system and the y flip with map()
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the pixel coordinates of a target point, including the y flip used when plotting a value, and confirm the result by placing a marker.
prerequisites: The Coordinate System section of Chapter 6
The map() function: map(value, fromLow, fromHigh, toLow, toHigh)

controls.label: Challenge
controls.action: Pose a new target: a height in whole meters on the dashed line x = N

controls.label: Clear markers
controls.action: Remove all markers and the current challenge

canvasInteractions: Pointer readout of mouseX and mouseY
Click to place a marker or answer a challenge

equations: y = map(heightMeters, 0, scaleMax, drawHeight, 0) = drawHeight - heightMeters / scaleMax * drawHeight
assumptions: A click within 12 pixels of the target counts as correct

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Calculate, then confirm by clicking, with worked feedback showing the filled-in map() call
keyQuestions: Where is (0, 0) on a p5.js canvas?
Why are the last two arguments of map() written drawHeight, 0 and not 0, drawHeight?
commonMisconceptions: y grows upward as on a mathematics graph
map(h, 0, max, 0, drawHeight) plots a height correctly
The origin is at the center of the canvas
assessmentOpportunities: Challenges correct out of challenges attempted
Written map() call for a new scale and height
